title: CsNAC8 positively regulates C6 aroma biosynthesis by activating key genes of the lipoxygenase pathway in cucumber fruits under supplemental lighting ‡
content:
Abstract
The freshness of cucumber fruits mainly results from the 6-carbon compounds (C6 aroma), which exhibit a unique flavor. Actually, the aroma content is greatly affected by environmental factors. However, how light affects C6 content in cucumber and its regulatory mechanism remain unknown. In this study, we found that C6 aroma content in cucumber fruits increased significantly under supplemental LED lighting with a red-to-blue ratio of 3:1. The expression of CsLOX01, the first key enzyme gene in the lipoxygenase pathway, increased significantly by 89.81% to 99.22% and positively correlated with the C6 aroma content. C6 aroma content was significantly enhanced 2 to 16 times in CsLOX01 overexpression cucumber lines. Transcription factors were screened based on a coexpression network constructed by integrating C6 aroma content and transcriptomic data, and 13 candidate transcription factors were highly correlated with C6 aroma content; among them, the NAC factor CsNAC8 increased by 37.56% under supplemental LED lighting. CsNAC8 was found to bind directly to the CGTG motif of the promoters of CsLOX01, 13-CsHPL, and CsADH7, as identified through dual-luciferase, yeast 1-hybrid, and electrophoretic mobility shift assays. C6 aroma content increased significantly by 12.69% to 51.26%, and the expression of CsLOX01, 13-CsHPL, and CsADH7 was significantly enhanced in the CsNAC8 overexpression cucumber lines, as verified by chromatin immunoprecipitation–quantitative PCR. A model was established and elucidated that CsNAC8 positively regulated C6 aroma biosynthesis by activating key genes of the lipoxygenase pathway in cucumber fruits under supplemental lighting.
